failure_modes.mode: Coil blockage due to DMF hydrolysis or salt precipitation
failure_modes.cause: Trace moisture in DMF or reaction byproducts (salts) precipitating in the narrow 0.75 mm ID coil at 120°C over long residence times (48 min)
failure_modes.mitigation: Implement rigorous solvent drying (molecular sieves) and install a 5 µm inline filter before the reactor; design for easy coil replacement

failure_modes.cause: High viscosity of DMF at 120°C combined with low flow rate (0.053 mL/min) and potential vapor pressure issues if inlet pressure drops below 2.66 bar
failure_modes.mitigation: Use a heated feed reservoir pressurized to >3 bar; employ a syringe pump with high precision and low pulsation; monitor inlet pressure continuously

failure_modes.mode: Thermal runaway due to heat transfer limitation
failure_modes.cause: Although Da_thermal is low, the long coil length (5.76 m) and low flow rate may lead to hot spots if the heating bath fails or if exotherm is underestimated
failure_modes.mitigation: Install multiple temperature sensors along the coil; implement an emergency quench valve and cooling system; verify heat transfer coefficients experimentally

single_points_of_failure: Back Pressure Regulator (BPR) — failure leads to pressure drop and potential solvent boiling
Syringe Pump — failure stops flow, leading to localized overheating and potential decomposition
validation_experiments: Run blank DMF at 120°C and 6.7 bar for 10 hours; monitor pressure stability and check for coil blockage or degradation
Perform a step-change test in flow rate (±10%) to assess system response and pressure stability
Conduct a thermal runaway simulation by abruptly increasing bath temperature by 20°C and monitoring reactor temperature response
